strengths: Strong Mathematical Foundation: The paper introduces three novel, mathematically elegant families of scalar bijections (Cubic Rational, Sinh Conjugation, Cubic Conjugation) that are globally smooth (C^\infty), analytically invertible in closed form, and defined on the entire real line. This elegantly resolves the trade-off between smoothness, analytical invertibility, and global domain.

Comprehensive and Diverse Evaluation: The authors evaluate their methods across a wide range of tasks: 1D toy tasks, 2D coupling and radial flows, standard image density estimation (CIFAR-10), tabular datasets (UCI), and a high-dimensional physics application (\phi^4 lattice field theory).

Downstream Benefits of Smoothness Evaluated: The paper explicitly demonstrates the benefits of global smoothness in Section B.3, showing a 1445\times reduction in second-derivative mean squared error (MSE) compared to rational-quadratic splines, and a 20\times reduction in training-loss variance. This is highly significant for scientific machine learning applications.

Novel Radial Flow Architecture: The radial flow architecture with angular dependence parametrized via Fourier series is clever, highly parameter-efficient (matching coupling flows with 1000\times fewer parameters on radial targets), and visually interpretable.

Excellent Clarity and Presentation: The paper is exceptionally well-written, with high-quality figures, detailed proofs of bijectivity constraints, and open-source code provided in the `bijx` library.
weaknesses: Computational Scaling with Expressivity: To increase expressivity, the proposed bijections must be stacked (N times), which scales the computational cost linearly with N. In contrast, for spline flows, one can increase the number of knots with almost flat computational overhead (as shown in Figure 21). At higher stack counts (N > 8), the proposed analytic bijections become computationally more expensive than RQ-Splines.

Incremental Performance Improvements on Standard ML Benchmarks: While the proposed bijections show significant qualitative and stability benefits, the quantitative improvements in standard density estimation metrics (BPD on CIFAR-10, Log-Likelihood on UCI) are relatively modest compared to established spline baselines.

Dimensional Scaling of Radial Flows: As acknowledged by the authors, radial flows are primarily suited for targets with radial structure or lower-dimensional systems. Scaling them to very high dimensions while maintaining expressivity without standard coupling layers remains a challenge.

strengths: Introduces three novel, mathematically elegant, globally smooth ($C^\infty$) and analytically invertible scalar bijections that successfully resolve long-standing trade-offs in discrete normalizing flows (e.g., matching the invertibility of affine maps with the expressivity and local control of splines).

Provides a thorough theoretical formulation, showing how algebraic rational functions can be analytically inverted via Cardano's formula and how conjugation with monotonic functions (e.g., sinh) can be used to construct robust bijections.
Proposes 'radial flows' which offer excellent training stability, geometric interpretability, and superb parameter efficiency (up to 1000x fewer parameters) on targets with radial structures.

Exhibits a comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple domains, including 1D toy problems, standard tabular data (UCI), image generation (CIFAR-10), and a practical physics application ($\phi^4$ lattice field theory) where the smoothness ($C^\infty$) property yields major benefits for computing higher-order derivatives.

The paper is exceptionally well-written, with highly informative visualizations (e.g., Figures 1, 6, and 13) and a detailed appendix that carefully addresses numerical stability, initialization, and parameterizations.
weaknesses: Computational overhead: To achieve competitive expressivity, multiple copies of the proposed bijections must be composed (stacked). As demonstrated in Figure 21, the wall-clock time scales linearly with the stack count $N$, making them slower than rational-quadratic splines for $N \ge 4$ in the forward pass.

The performance gains on standard UCI tabular benchmarks (Table 3) are marginal, and on some datasets like HEPMASS and MINIBOONE, the proposed bijections do not consistently outperform the spline baselines.

While radial flows are elegant and highly effective for structured target densities, their design remains primarily limited to low-dimensional settings or problems with explicit coordinate decompositions, with limited general high-dimensional scaling.

strengths: The paper successfully addresses a long-standing trade-off in normalizing flows by proposing three novel families of scalar bijections that are simultaneously smooth (C^infinity), globally defined on R, and analytically invertible in closed form.

The introduction of radial flows with angular dependence (via Fourier series) is creative, highly interpretable, and exceptionally parameter-efficient for distributions with radial or spherical geometries.

Strong and diverse empirical validation spanning multiple domains: 1D/2D synthetic targets, standard tabular/image benchmarks (UCI, CIFAR-10), and a high-dimensional physics application (phi^4 lattice field theory).

Excellent analysis of the downstream practical benefits of C^infinity smoothness (Appendix B.3), demonstrating that the proposed bijections exhibit dramatically lower errors in higher-order derivatives and reduced training-loss variance compared to piecewise-smooth spline alternatives.
weaknesses: To increase expressivity, the proposed analytic bijections must be stacked sequentially. Because wall-clock time scales linearly with the stack depth, they become computationally more expensive than spline flows (which have flat scaling with respect to the number of knots) at moderate stack depths.

The applicability of radial flows is primarily restricted to low-dimensional spaces or targets with specific geometric symmetries, as scaling angular-dependent radial flows to high dimensions suffers from the curse of dimensionality.
